videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: camera-height sweep, -1 to +1 m (no real frame)
videos.shown: (no real frame) | recorded real frame at 0 m | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: Lower or higher cameras (a sports car, a truck) see the road at a different angle. There is no real frame at another height, so this is a visual check only; the report scores the road region against a road-plane warp (RESULTS section 12) and against real car/scooter pairs on MV2.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: EUVS / MARS location 41: different route through the same place (transfer)
videos.shown: real test frame | raw splat | released Difix-ref | NVIDIA Fixer | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net
videos.caption: The test traversal takes another route through the same place (median 5.5 m and 89 deg from the nearest training camera). Only the released, generically trained fixers help here; our Para-Lane-trained models do not transfer (RESULTS section 13).
videos.attribution: Data: EUVS benchmark (ICCV 2025) MARS scenes (MARS, CVPR 2024; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). CS 566, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: heading sweep, -15 to +15 deg
videos.shown: real frame rotated by the exact homography (black = never seen by the real camera) | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: For a pure rotation the real frame can be warped exactly; black regions are parts of the scene the recorded camera never saw. Inside the seen region every method stays close to the real frame (heading is not what breaks the splat); the newly revealed regions at the image border are where splats and fixers improvise.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.
videos.real_ground_truth: exact inside the region the recorded camera saw (black outside)

videos.title: HUGSIM nuScenes scene-0167: closed loop, LTF policy, no fixer
videos.shown: policy's three front camera views + bird's-eye view (ego, other vehicles, planned path)
videos.caption: One closed-loop rollout (hard scenario, seed 0): HD-Score 0.78, route completion 1.00. Played at 5 fps (sim runs at 4 Hz). Across 25 scenarios x 3 seeds the no-fixer HD-Score is 0.41 (RESULTS section 8).
videos.attribution: Data: HUGSIM released nuScenes scenes (MIT); nuScenes by Motional, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. CS 566, non-commercial.

videos.title: HUGSIM nuScenes scene-0064: ego car shifted 0 -> 3 m (no real frame)
videos.scenario: lateral offset in a released simulator scene
videos.shown: (no real frame) | raw HUGSIM render | released Difix | NVIDIA Fixer | Difix-FT | our U-Net
videos.caption: HUGSIM's released reconstruction rendered 0-3 m off the logged path. Detector agreement with the 0 m render falls ~16% by 3 m; NVIDIA Fixer recovers most, our Para-Lane-trained models do not transfer (our U-Net washes out vehicles; RESULTS section 8).
videos.attribution: Data: HUGSIM released nuScenes scenes (MIT); nuScenes by Motional, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. CS 566, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: lane-change sweep, 0 -> 3 -> 6 m
videos.shown: nearest real frame (only on the two real lanes) | raw | released Difix | our Difix (ref) | our U-Net | road prior | progressive splat
videos.caption: The camera slides from the recorded lane to the next lane (3.3 m) and the one after (6.2 m). Real frames exist only where Para-Lane actually drove (shown as the nearest real frame of that lane, driven at another time, so traffic differs); in between there is no ground truth.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.
videos.real_ground_truth: partial: only at the two real adjacent lanes (another pass, traffic differs)

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_14 (new test road): curve, two lanes over (median 5.3 m)
videos.scenario: lateral offset, curved road (new test scene)
videos.shown: real far-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: scene_14 was added as a held-out test scene (never used for training or selection): the road bends by 30-50 deg over ~110 m (per pass). Lane 0's splat is rendered where lane 2 drove. Our driving-trained Difix draws crisp lane lines, but not always where the real ones are (compare the markings with the real frame): plausible is not the same as faithful. Per-scene numbers: RESULTS section 15. Marks (same rules as the metrics): orange = invented lane paint, blue = erased lane paint, red box = spurious vehicle.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_17: straight road, two lanes over (median 7.8 m)
videos.shown: real far-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: About 7.8 m from the recorded lane, the splat has never seen most of the road surface. Every fixer produces a cleaner-looking image, but none recovers the real lane geometry reliably; lane agreement stays low (RESULTS section 5). Marks (same rules as the metrics): orange = invented lane paint, blue = erased lane paint, red box = spurious vehicle.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: straight road, one lane over (median 3.3 m)
videos.shown: real adjacent-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: The splat was fitted on lane 0 only and is rendered where lane 1 actually drove. Released Difix sharpens but does not restore the missing lane paint; our driving-trained Difix restores most lane lines; the small U-Net changes little. Cars differ between passes (the lanes were driven at different times). Marks (same rules as the metrics): orange = invented lane paint, blue = erased lane paint, red box = spurious vehicle.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_15 (new test road): under a highway, one lane over (median 4.1 m)
videos.scenario: lateral offset, shadows + traffic (new test scene)
videos.shown: real adjacent-lane frame | raw splat | released Difix | our Difix reimplementation (ref) | our U-Net | NVIDIA Fixer
videos.caption: scene_15 (held-out test scene) runs under an elevated highway: hard shadows, pillars and the most traffic of all Para-Lane scenes we used. Vehicles are pasted from the real frame only for the metrics, not here: cars in the renders are whatever the splat and fixer produce (the lanes were driven at different times). Per-scene numbers: RESULTS section 15. Marks (same rules as the metrics): orange = invented lane paint, blue = erased lane paint, red box = spurious vehicle.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: progressive 3D update, before / after (median 3.3 m)
videos.shown: real | original splat | refined without fixer (control) | progressive with Difix-FT | progressive with our Difix
videos.caption: The splat itself is refined with fixed pseudo-views at +-3 m and +-6 m (Difix3D+ progressive update), then rendered WITHOUT any fixer. On scene_16 the lane lines come back in 3D (lane F1 0.18 -> 0.90 at ~3 m); on scene_17 the same procedure helps far less, so this gain is scene-dependent.
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

videos.title: Para-Lane scene_16: road-surface prior, before / after (median 3.3 m)
videos.shown: real | raw splat | splat fitted with the LiDAR road-surface prior
videos.caption: A height/slope field fitted to LiDAR pulls road Gaussians onto the road plane and flattens them. No image generator is involved; lane lines are sharper off-path, while the splat's other errors remain (spurious vehicles one lane over: 0.061 per image, against 0.064 for the raw render).
videos.attribution: Data: Para-Lane (Ni et al., 3DV 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Renders/fixes: CS 566 course project, non-commercial.

about: Demo clips of the CS 566 (UW-Madison, Fall 2026) course project 'How far off the recorded path can a Gaussian-splat driving simulator be trusted?' (Kyle Sha, Allen Xia). Non-commercial, educational use. Each entry carries its dataset attribution; no raw datasets or model weights are distributed. Labels are burned into every frame; tiles without a real frame say so.
format: H.264 (libx264, yuv420p, faststart) MP4, 1280 px wide, <= 20 s, <= 4.5 MB; stills JPEG <= 500 KB
